chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever buys an animal, its back (for riding) would be for him, and upon Allah would be its sustenance.'

key_terms.دَابَّة: A riding/pack animal, commonly a horse, donkey, or mule; any quadruped used for transport in classical Arabic
key_terms.رِزْق: Provision, sustenance, livelihood — here attributed to Allah as the guarantor of the animal's feed and care
key_terms.ظَهْر: The back (of an animal), used idiomatically for the right to ride or use the animal

ai.seo_question: In Islam, who is responsible for providing for an animal's sustenance when it is purchased?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a concise legal and theological principle regarding the purchase of riding animals: the buyer acquires the right to use the animal's back for transport, while Allah takes upon Himself the responsibility of providing for its sustenance. This hadith reflects the classical Shia jurisprudential understanding that ownership of an animal's labor does not negate the divine covenant of provision, reinforcing trust in God (tawakkul) as the ultimate provider for all living creatures.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Ja’far Bin bashir, from Dawood Al Raqy who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who buys an animal, its back (for riding) would be for him, and upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup> would be its sustenance’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ja‘far ibn Bashir from Dawud al- Riqqiy who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘If one buys a stumper, he has the benefit of riding and its sustenance is with Allah.’”
